target_customer: Multifamily property managers and rental operators who need to convert leads to tours and leases
problem: Rental leads go cold when nobody replies quickly outside business hours. Zuma used an AI texting agent named Kelsey to answer, qualify and book tours, handing off to humans when needed.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per property or unit, with human assisted AI service

founders.name: Shiv Gettu
previous_startups: Astro (short term rental property company, started 2018)
founders.background_notes: Former real estate consultant per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Kendrick Bradley
previous_startups: Astro (short term rental property company, started 2018)
founders.background_notes: Left SpaceX in 2018 to join a property management company, per TechCrunch.

technical_complexity.rationale: A 2021 conversational lead agent needed property data integrations and human handoff. Language models were not yet general purpose, so quality came from scripted flows plus human review.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with property systems and trained conversation data help, but lead texting was easy to copy and LLMs later lowered the barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: EliseAI and others competed for years. Venn acquired Zuma for 50 million dollars in September 2026.

market_need_then: Zuma reported 10 times revenue growth since January 2021 and a pilot with Bungalow showing 2.1 times conversion and 35 times return in 2021, after the pandemic turned its founders' short term rental business into a leasing office model.

branding.domain_note: Uses getzuma.com, a get prefix domain, not zuma.com. The legal entity is Resident Boost Inc.

identity.logo: Stylized geometric mark beside the wordmark
identity.mascot_or_character: Kelsey, the named AI leasing agent persona
identity.voice_and_tone: Customizable to feel like a member of the client's team

branding.brand_signature: Kelsey, the named AI leasing assistant

rebrands.why: Not stated. The legal entity name and YC URL slug remain resident-boost and the website privacy policy names Resident Boost Inc. d/b/a Zuma

branding.community_and_virality: Bisnow sponsored coverage and customer case studies. No fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A short memorable name and a named agent persona make the product easy to explain, but no evidence of brand driven growth beyond a normal B2B funnel.

pivots.from: Astro, a tech driven short term rental property company
pivots.to: Virtual leasing office with AI text agent
pivots.why: The pandemic halted travel demand, per TechCrunch

outcome_analysis: Zuma emerged from a pandemic pivot of a short term rental firm into an AI leasing texting agent, raised a 6.7 million dollar a16z led seed in November 2021 with strong early conversion metrics, grew into voice and collections, and was acquired by Venn in September 2026 for a reported 50 million dollars. The outcome is a moderate strategic exit rather than a large one, in a crowded category with EliseAI as a main rival.
notes: The Series A claims (Feb 2024 on VCBacked, Mar 2025 on Caplight) and totals raised ranging 6.83 to 18.33 million dollars are single aggregator figures and not recorded as rounds. The 50 million price is consistent across Commercial Observer, Calcalist and Pulse 2.0. Founders' earlier firm Astro is named in a search snippet and TechCrunch refers to an unnamed hospitality company. Competitors in 2021 were not named in TechCrunch and the search returned later (2024 to 2026) lists, so the list is empty. Whether Resident Boost was the original brand name is not stated, only the legal entity and slug.
